<reason>A offered the stronger decision rule: competent patients retain presumptive authority, while concrete competing obligations can justify limits. B raised meaningful challenges involving dementia and harmful interventions, but A answered them directly. B repeatedly treated any exception as disproving greater weight and relabeled safety, welfare, and professional obligations as dignity without establishing that equivalence. A also answered B’s treatment-refusal concession by showing that competing interpretations of dignity still require a rule allocating authority.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s distinction between authority over one’s body and entitlement to a clinician’s participation substantially weakened B’s intervention examples. Combined with the point that grounding a right does not establish priority over it, this exposed the central gap in B’s argument rather than merely conceding exceptions.</best_rebuttal>
